title: Product identity for translated sign encodings
statement: Let $f:\mathbb F_2^n\to\mathbb F_2$ be a Boolean function, and let $x,y,y'\in\mathbb F_2^n$. Encode a bit $b$ as the real sign $(-1)^b$. Then the product of the real sign encodings of $f(x+y)$ and $f(x+y')$ equals the real sign encoding, evaluated at $x$, of the function $z\mapsto f(z+y)+f(z+y')$, with addition in $\mathbb F_2^n$ and $\mathbb F_2$, respectively.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on $\mathbb F_2^n$
